nodes.title: Stroke-sequential composition gate on the persistent canvas
nodes.motivation: Test the painter hypothesis: because the write bandwidth per pass is bounded by M*edges, sequential passes onto a persistent canvas, each conditioned on the accumulated field and the write step, should accumulate detail the way iterative refinement does, instead of stamping one attractor.

nodes.title: Event-norm port angle replaces the reflection-locked pointwise law
nodes.motivation: The first real joint updates showed the write port stuck near total reflection (acceptance 0.57% falling to 3-6%, write angle 0.036-0.12 rad over 440 updates): the angle consumed the per-site innovation magnitude, so a unit-norm token's innovation is grid-and-channel averaged down to ~0.04 and the initial admittance 0.69 could only ever produce ~0.036 rad. Opening the port would require the admittance to grow more than tenfold for numerical reasons, locking the training direction regardless of what the predictor learns.
nodes.action: Abandoned the affected run at step 440 and replaced the angle law: theta_c = atan(Y_c * ||delta||_Pi) with ||delta||_Pi the precision-weighted event-total innovation norm (site-averaged, hence grid-resolution independent), and the unit direction delta/||delta||_Pi as the incident mode, implemented in a division-free form that is smooth at zero innovation. Null innovation remains the exact identity rotation; accepted_fraction is now the Pi-weighted transmission of the unit incident mode, and the raw incident/reflected/accepted energies remain the boundary ledger. Logged innovation_norm and write_admittance_mean per step so prior quality, innovation size, and admittance can be distinguished while training.
nodes.conclusion: Structural only: exact rotation ledger on (field, unit incident mode), exact identity at zero innovation, resolution-independent event norm and angle across grids, and at the registered d=128 calibration an unpredictable token has ||delta||_Pi ~ 1 giving a finite exchange at initial admittance. No capability claim; the joint 3000-update rerun must show whether the opened port improves NLL, write free energy, and readout accuracy together.
issues: Precision growth raises ||delta||_Pi for the same physical innovation; the joint dynamics must regulate admittance and precision rather than the angle saturating.

The transmitted amplitude saturates at one unit-norm mode per event, so a single event can never overwrite the field arbitrarily; the resulting NESS field level is higher than under the closed port and must be watched for stability.
accepted_fraction semantics changed to the unit-mode transmission; comparisons with the abandoned run's acceptance numbers are not like-for-like.
The event norm is exactly resolution independent only through the chart's per-mode RMS normalization; the writer's channel_scale calibration still sets the dimensionless unit at d=128.
nodes.invalidation: Reject this fix if, at unit event norms, the port still cannot open (transmission stays near zero across training) or if opening destabilizes token NLL instead of reducing it.
nodes.confidence_note: Scale mismatch was measured on the first 440 real updates; the replacement law is unit-tested structurally. The training consequence is unverified until the rerun reports.

nodes.title: W2-modern arm isolating the write factor on the settled integrator
nodes.motivation: With the integrator (K=16, dt=4*tau0, T=64*tau0), bath (unified), chunk (32), readout (kernel_r1) and steering (continuous directions) now fixed, the single blocking question for the main architecture is the write: W2 impedance (direct token-conditioned content) versus W4 predictive innovation port.
nodes.action: Run 3000 registered updates of W2 write with the exact hybrid read/steer/integrator bundle via the reference trainer extended with --tau-0; adaptive clock off to match the hybrid.
nodes.conclusion: Rejected the write hypothesis with the opposite sign. Under the single standalone registered evaluator the W2-modern arm scores 7.8922 (best checkpoint, step 3000) versus the W4 line's published 7.4203 - the W4 predictive-innovation write BEATS the W2 direct content write by 0.47 nats under identical modern conditions (same readout, steering, integrator, bath and chunk). The 0.205-nat gap to the archived Continuous-Q8 baseline is therefore attributable to tuning maturity (no lr schedule, excluded adaptive clock, still-descending trajectory at 2500), not the write law. Note: the reference trainer's in-loop validation (7.611) differs from the standalone registered evaluator (7.8922); the published number is the protocol-consistent one.
issues: The W2 line lacks the posterior precision state; if W2 wins on NLL, the T and M roadmap needs either a precision state added to W2 or a hybrid write law.
The entropy-gated dual port (direct content gated by predictor uncertainty with a description-length cost) remains the principled combination if both factors prove real.
The old champion's adaptive clock is excluded here for parity; its individual contribution is unmeasured.
nodes.invalidation: The write-factor explanation is rejected if this arm lands within 0.05 nats of the hybrid's projected endpoint.

nodes.title: Main architecture declared: the W4 predictive-innovation port line
nodes.motivation: After the completed registered arms (unified-bath K16 run, hybrid read/steer arm, W2-modern write arm) and the causal-attribution and two-axis probes, the write factor is decided with the opposite sign of the working hypothesis and the main architecture can be declared.
nodes.action: Fix the main line as: CBIM torus field with collision-centric dynamics; W4 predictive-innovation write port (categorical prior, factorized chart, event-norm admittance law, persistent channelwise posterior precision, single field write path); K=16 integration steps at dt=4*tau0 preserving event duration T=64*tau0; unified three-layer field-only bath; BPTT chunk 32; fixed D3Q8 transport (continuous steering optional for early-convergence speed only); kernel_r1 readout for pragmatic NLL or belief_agent readout where the strict field-only instrument matters. Publish both records and pursue the remaining gap to the archived baseline (7.2154) and GDN-2 (6.4981) through training maturity (lr schedule, longer runs, adaptive-clock integration) rather than architecture redesign.
nodes.conclusion: Structural declaration backed by completed registered evidence: the W4 line beats the W2 write by 0.47 nats under identical conditions, matches the belief/kernel readout asymptotically, and its integrator and memory budget are measured optima. Best registered score 7.4203 versus 7.2154 (archived baseline) and 6.4981 (GDN-2); no capability claim over GDN-2.
issues: Training maturity is the remaining gap: the v4 trajectory was still descending at 2500 with a constant learning rate; lr decay and longer runs are the first lever.
The adaptive clock of the archived champion was excluded from all comparison arms and its individual contribution is unmeasured.
The posterior precision state inflates with training (mean ~55 by step 3000); the T action must condition on normalized signals.
Transport is causally idle at evaluation time in both lines; its training-time role and a possible transport-light variant are open.
The T duration action and M-path posterior remain the next capability stages on the declared main line.
nodes.invalidation: Reopen the architecture if training-maturity levers fail to move the W4 line below 7.2, or if a registered variant beats it by more than 0.1 nats at equal budget.
nodes.confidence_note: Main architecture chosen from completed registered comparisons at equal budget on one GPU and one dataset; the maturity levers for the remaining gap are untested.
